dedupe_keys.name: gnpy optical route planning library gaussian noise model

description: GNPy is an open-source, community-developed Python library from the Telecom Infra Project's Open Optical and Packet Transport group for building route planning and optimisation tools for real mesh optical (DWDM) networks. It computes signal propagation along a light path with the Gaussian Noise model of fibre nonlinearity, with fibre and Raman fibre spans, EDFA and multiband amplifier models, ROADMs, transceivers and their receiver constraints, and reports generalised SNR, OSNR and Q-margin per channel, so feasibility of services on a network can be checked. Networks are described as JSON or Excel topologies with an equipment library, fully specified or partially designed for auto-design; scripts gnpy-transmission-example and gnpy-path-request run single paths or batches of service requests, and outputs follow YANG-compatible formats. Coverage: any optical network a user describes, with example networks. Format and access: Python package on PyPI and Docker images, source on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence, documentation on Read the Docs; version 3.0 was released on Zenodo on 3 September 2026. Caveats: quality depends on equipment parameters, many of which are vendor-specific; it is a physical-layer planning tool, not a traffic simulator; v3.0 changed channel numbering. Simulation uses: capacity planning, optimisation of optical backbones and the effect of link or amplifier failures on reachable services. Related records: the PCFM optical link GSNR calculator and PASSION WDM planner are research tools on the same layer.
